title: The last letter
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, quiet old American town in late winter, rain-slick brick streets and gaslight-style lamps, vintage cream envelopes with red wax seals and dried roses, faded rose and slate blue tones, adults only, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 4. Happy Valentine's. Meet me where we said. 💘

Original fiction. Part 5 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Ben found Thomas, eighty, by the river, and handed him Evelyn's letter. Then Thomas asked what year Ben thought it was.
scenes.image: an old man on a bench by a foggy river holding a cream letter

scenes.narration: Ben laughed, and told him. Thomas just nodded slowly, like a man doing math he didn't like.
scenes.image: an old man nodding slowly, eyes far away, river mist around him

scenes.narration: Every day that week, a new letter. Every day, Ben carried it to the bench. Thomas read each one twice, then folded it into his coat.
scenes.image: a stack of cream envelopes with red wax seals tied with a faded ribbon

scenes.narration: This morning, Valentine's Day, the last one came. It was heavier. Inside was a pressed red rose.
scenes.image: a pressed red rose falling out of an opened cream envelope onto a wooden table

scenes.narration: My dearest Thomas. Meet me where we said. Valentine's night. I'll wear the red coat. I'll wait as long as it takes. Love, Evelyn.
scenes.image: a red wool coat hanging on a hook beside a rain-streaked window at night

scenes.narration: Thomas knew where. The old mill bridge. He was going to ask her to marry him there. Fifty-two years ago tonight.
scenes.image: an old stone mill bridge over a dark river at night, a single lamp at its center

scenes.narration: I never made it, he said. There was an ice storm. I remember the headlights. I don't remember getting home.
scenes.image: headlights glaring through a freezing rainstorm on a dark country road

scenes.narration: Ben said he'd drive him. Tonight. Whatever was waiting there, Thomas shouldn't face it alone.
scenes.image: a mail carrier holding open a car door on a wet street at night

scenes.narration: Thomas got in. He smelled like rain and old roses. He held the ring box in both hands the whole way.
scenes.image: an old man's hands holding a small velvet ring box in the dim light of a car

scenes.narration: At a red light, Ben glanced in the rearview mirror. The passenger seat was empty. But beside him, he could still hear Thomas breathing.
scenes.image: a rearview mirror reflecting an empty passenger seat, red traffic light glowing through rain
